newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian palace reports death threats against king.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian palace reports death threats against king.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk has been sent death threats and expatriate Cambodians have warned of an assassination bid, a palace release seen on Monday said.

The compilers of Sihanouk's monthly bulletin, in an interview with the king on Sunday, suggested recent threatening letters to the king were linked to articles in their Monthly Bulletin of Documentation (BMD).
They said the threats were designed to make the BMD "renounce its independence of spirit, to shut up and even disappear".
The BMD is a collection of press articles, letters and commentary by the king.
Sihanouk, noting his bulletin had been closed by the Maoist Khmer Rouge during their brutal 1975-79 "killing fields" rule, said he would suspend publication if asked by the country's "strongmen".

"I am ready to do what our STRONGMEN ask me to do concerning the BMD," he wrote. "If they want to imitate (Khmer Rouge leader) Khieu Samphan by asking me formally and officially to suspend sine die the running of the BMD, I will agree to obey them."

Cambodia is run by an uneasy coalition of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and the formerly communist Cambodian People's Party of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who is regarded as the country's strongman.
The BMD interviewers quoted unnamed Cambodians living in France as warning the king of an attempt on his life.
The king is in Beijing recovering from eye surgery.

Sihanouk played a pivotal role in winning an end to the country's long civil war as the only figure able to command the respect of the world community and the four factions, including the radical Khmer Rouge guerrilla group, that agreed to peace in 1991 after 21 years of strife.
